reason: Both bullets under Certificate renewal on the ALB certificates page state the ACM automatic renewal and the duty to monitor and renew an imported ACM certificate before it expires.

The action types page lists forward, redirect, fixed-response and jwt-validation with the quoted descriptions, and the Action basics bullet gives the HTTPS user authentication plus routing action sentence; the claim says include, so other types do not contradict it.
Under Application-based stickiness the target is expected to set a custom cookie, the ALB generates an encrypted application cookie, and the name the client sees begins with AWSALBAPP-.
ATW does anomaly detection on every ALB, mitigation reduces traffic to anomalous targets, and the Requirement line says mitigation is only available with the Weighted random algorithm.
The gRPC considerations list the three only-supported items (HTTPS, forward, instance and ip) and the action types page says gRPC or HTTP/2 allow only forward actions; scope matches.

Health check logs page states optional and disabled by default, compressed files in the specified S3 bucket, S3 storage charged but not bandwidth, and the Important note on CloudWatch Logs delivery to CloudWatch Logs, Firehose or S3.
Create an HTTPS listener page states at least one SSL server certificate, termination of the front-end connection and decryption before targets, and a required security policy.
Prepare the Lambda function section says the console adds the permissions to the function policy and that with the AWS CLI you must use add-permission to grant ELB permission to invoke.

The LCU Details list on the ELB pricing page (with rule evaluations and Lambda GB, so the ALB LCU) gives 25 new connections per second, and Note 1 gives the RSA <=2K and ECDSA <=256 condition for HTTPS listeners.
The Certificates quota table on the ALB quotas page shows Maximum certificate chain depth 4 with Adjustable No, under the sentence naming CA certificates and revocation lists.
The same Certificates quota table shows TLS message size 64 K, Adjustable No.
The ELB FAQ answer to which load balancer to select states the sentence about third-party virtual appliances and Gateway Load Balancer verbatim.

Under the Network Load Balancer FAQ section, the question on new connections/flows per sec versus requests/sec is answered No, multiple requests can be sent in a single connection; the LCU context is in the same section.
Target security groups section of the GWLB register targets page gives both the no-security-group sentence with the IP-address consequence and the port 6081 rule for registered EC2 instances.
The identical sentence appears on both the ALB and NLB target group pages: per target group, default settings unless overridden at creation or modified later.

Both the ALB and NLB target type sections state the primary private IP for instance ID targets and any private IP from one or more network interfaces for IP targets, enabling the same port for multiple applications.

Both pages state you can't specify publicly routable IP addresses and list the VPC subnets plus four CIDR blocks; calling the block list private is a mild paraphrase (100.64.0.0/10 is RFC 6598) but does not change the meaning.
The capacity reservation pages for ALB, NLB and GWLB state the static minimum, continued scaling up and down above it, and the upcoming event with a sudden traffic spike use case.
Registered targets section on both the ALB and NLB target group pages contains the sentence verbatim.
NLB Deregistration delay section states the 300 second default to unused, that the value can be changed, the at least 120 seconds recommendation, and that QUIC is always 300 and not adjustable.
The NLB FAQ answer comparing NLB with the Classic TCP listener states source IP preservation not in Classic, a static IP per AZ and assigning an Elastic IP per AZ.
NLB quota table row Targets per Network Load Balancer is 3,000 with Adjustable Yes, and footnote 3 gives the 500 per load balancer maximum when cross-zone load balancing is enabled.
NLB Target type section lists instance, ip and alb and states that with alb you can register a single Application Load Balancer.
Data protection page, Encryption in transit, states the three sentences verbatim.
ALB security policies page states AWS recommends the two named PQ-TLS policies; scope is ALB.

The ALB forward actions section gives weight 0 to 999 per target group and the NLB listeners section gives 0 to 999 and that weight 0 receives no traffic; the claim attributes the weight-0 statement to the NLB guide.
